newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African gold stocks surge, JSE at fresh peak.
newsitem.headline: S.African gold stocks surge, JSE at fresh peak.

text.p: South African gold stocks, virtually ignored in recent weeks, stole the limelight on gains in bullion late on Friday hoisting the all-share index to a fresh record peak and Western Areas up some 16 percent.

Platinum stocks powered ahead, taking the world's biggest producer Rusplats up 3.5 percent to a new 79 rand year high, as the white metal fixed at its highest level since 1990 amid a lack of world supplies.
At the close the all gold index was up over three percent or 35.3 points to 1,175.6.
But industrial stocks, which surged over 230 points this weak following a surprise leap in May official reserves, came off their highs on profit-taking in the afternoon.
The industrial ended up only 6.8 points at 8,476.7.

Dealers said robust gains in platinum stocks could be shortlived if the Russians began supplying the market again. There were rumours that they may start again in June when their export licences were in place.

The bank-laced financial index stormed to yet another new peak, up 93.1 points to 9,619.3, on the promise of an easing in pressures on margins if local interest rates were cut within the next few months, as was rumoured in the equity market.
Overall market gains pushed the all-share index to its second consecutive closing high of 7,262.2, a gain of 43.7 points.
The market was seen strong again next week riding on rate cut talk as well as continued foreign and institutional interest.
